*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: out/analyze.py
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib
+matplotlib.use("Agg")
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+OUT = Path("out")
+WEEKDAYS = ["Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday"]
+con = duckdb.connect()
+crashes = con.execute("""
+    SELECT crash_date, count(*) AS crash_count
+    FROM read_parquet('./data/crashes.parquet')
+    WHERE crash_date >= DATE '2013-01-01' AND crash_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
+    GROUP BY crash_date
+""").df()
+crashes["weekday_num"] = pd.to_datetime(crashes["crash_date"]).dt.weekday
+by_weekday = crashes.groupby("weekday_num")["crash_count"].sum().reindex(range(7), fill_value=0)
+
+dates = pd.date_range("2013-01-01", "2025-12-31", freq="D")
+exposure = pd.Series(dates.weekday).value_counts().reindex(range(7), fill_value=0).sort_index()
+total = int(by_weekday.sum())
+df = pd.DataFrame({
+    "weekday": WEEKDAYS,
+    "crashes": by_weekday.astype(int).to_numpy(),
+    "share_percent": (by_weekday / total * 100).to_numpy(),
+    "calendar_dates": exposure.astype(int).to_numpy(),
+})
+df["crashes_per_calendar_date"] = df["crashes"] / df["calendar_dates"]
+
+options = [
+    {
+        "id": 1,
+        "metric": "Number of police-reported crashes",
+        "denominator": "None; total crashes in the 2013–2025 date range",
+        "grouping": "Day of week of crash_date, Monday through Sunday",
+        "chart_type": "Vertical bar chart",
+        "reason": "Raw counts directly show how many reported crashes occurred on each weekday over the full period.",
+        "probability": 0.5,
+        "answer": "Friday had the most crashes (338,800) and Sunday the fewest (257,544) from 2013 through 2025.",
+        "interpretation": "This framing answers how the total number of crashes is distributed across weekdays, with Friday the highest and Sunday the lowest. Raw totals are a direct description of the requested period, but do not adjust for the slightly different number of calendar dates falling on each weekday.",
+    },
+    {
+        "id": 2,
+        "metric": "Share of all police-reported crashes",
+        "denominator": "All crashes with crash_date in 2013–2025 (2,132,218 crashes)",
+        "grouping": "Day of week of crash_date, Monday through Sunday",
+        "chart_type": "Vertical bar chart",
+        "reason": "Percent shares make each weekday's contribution to all crashes in the period easy to compare.",
+        "probability": 0.3,
+        "answer": "Friday accounted for the largest share of crashes (15.89%), while Sunday accounted for the smallest (12.08%).",
+        "interpretation": "This framing answers what fraction of the period's reported crashes fell on each weekday, with Friday contributing the most and Sunday the least. The denominator makes the percentages directly comparable as parts of the total, but this remains a composition of recorded crashes rather than a weekday-specific risk rate.",
+    },
+    {
+        "id": 3,
+        "metric": "Average police-reported crashes per calendar date",
+        "denominator": "Number of calendar dates of each weekday in 2013–2025",
+        "grouping": "Day of week of crash_date, Monday through Sunday",
+        "chart_type": "Vertical bar chart",
+        "reason": "Dividing by the number of dates in the period adjusts for weekday exposure in the calendar.",
+        "probability": 0.2,
+        "answer": "On an average calendar date, Friday had 498.97 crashes and Sunday had 379.03, the highest and lowest weekday averages.",
+        "interpretation": "This framing answers how many crashes occurred per occurrence of each weekday, correcting for the small differences in weekday counts in the 2013–2025 calendar. Friday remains the highest and Sunday the lowest on this basis; the data do not provide traffic volume or exposure by road user, so these averages are not individual travel-risk rates.",
+    },
+]
+
+for option in options:
+    i = option["id"]
+    if i == 1:
+        values = df[["weekday", "crashes"]].copy()
+        ycol, ylabel = "crashes", "Number of crashes"
+    elif i == 2:
+        values = df[["weekday", "share_percent"]].copy()
+        ycol, ylabel = "share_percent", "Share of all crashes (%)"
+    else:
+        values = df[["weekday", "crashes", "calendar_dates", "crashes_per_calendar_date"]].copy()
+        ycol, ylabel = "crashes_per_calendar_date", "Crashes per calendar date"
+    values.to_csv(OUT / f"values_{i}.csv", index=False, float_format="%.6f")
+
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
+    bars = ax.bar(values["weekday"], values[ycol], color="#3977a8")
+    ax.set_title(["NYC crashes by weekday, 2013–2025", "Share of NYC crashes by weekday, 2013–2025", "Average NYC crashes per weekday date, 2013–2025"][i - 1])
+    ax.set_xlabel("Day of week")
+    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
+    ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
+    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
+    if i == 2:
+        ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(plt.FuncFormatter(lambda x, _: f"{x:.0f}%"))
+    for bar, value in zip(bars, values[ycol]):
+        label = f"{value:.2f}" if i == 3 else (f"{value:.2f}%" if i == 2 else f"{int(value):,}")
+        ax.annotate(label, (bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2, bar.get_height()), xytext=(0, 4), textcoords="offset points", ha="center", fontsize=8)
+    fig.tight_layout()
+    fig.savefig(OUT / f"option_{i}.png", dpi=160)
+    plt.close(fig)
+
+(OUT / "options.json").write_text(json.dumps({"options": options}, indent=2) + "\n")
+print(df.to_string(index=False))
+print(f"Total crashes: {total}; calendar dates by weekday: {exposure.to_dict()}")
*** End Patch

ANSWER:

By share of all 2,132,218 crashes, Friday was highest (15.89%) and Sunday lowest (12.08%).
